lead.headline: Labor Department suspends Microsoft, Adobe and major IT firms from PERM
lead.deck: The Department of Labor says it will not accept new or pending permanent labor certification applications involving the affected companies, citing alleged fraud and worker-displacement concerns. Announced October 8.
body: At an October 8 news conference, the U.S. Department of Labor announced that it will not accept new or pending permanent labor certification (PERM) applications involving Microsoft, Adobe and several major information-technology companies. PERM certification is ordinarily the first step in an employment-based green-card case, so a suspension reaches the sponsored workers of the named employers, not only the companies.

The Secretary of Labor, Keith Sonderling, framed the step as enforcement tied to allegations of fraud and to concerns that foreign workers are being used in ways that disadvantage U.S. workers; the written scope, the effective date and any duration were not detailed at the conference. At the same event, the Vice President said the administration would investigate nine universities over alleged abuse of a program for international students. Affected employers and workers should confirm the terms, and any individual effect, against the Department’s own notice before acting.
lead.src: Official source: U.S. Department of Labor — OFLC, Permanent Labor Certification ↗ · DOL ETA — Foreign Labor Certification news ↗ (confirm the written release on dol.gov)

items.title: Biometrics and continuous vetting: the proposed rule behind the FBI privacy notices applicants are receiving
items.deck: DHS/USCIS has proposed to broaden the collection and use of biometrics (RIN 1615-AC99; DHS Docket USCIS-2025-0205), moving toward continuous immigration vetting, under which biometrics may be checked against FBI…
body: DHS/USCIS has proposed to broaden the collection and use of biometrics (RIN 1615-AC99; DHS Docket USCIS-2025-0205), moving toward continuous immigration vetting, under which biometrics may be checked against FBI criminal-history records on an ongoing basis while a matter is pending. Separately, applicants whose fingerprints are submitted for a non-criminal-justice purpose receive the FBI Privacy Act and Non-Criminal Justice Applicant’s Privacy Rights notice required by 28 U.S.C. 534 and 28 C.F.R. § 50.12; the notice requires no action and explains how criminal-history records are collected, used, and shared. The rulemaking is a proposal; comments closed January 2, 2026.

lead.headline: DHS propõe taxa de US$70.000 para o OPT de estudantes F-1
lead.deck: Proposta publicada hoje prevê US$30.000 para OPT subsequente, como a extensão STEM; comentários até 09/11.
body: A proposta do ICE/DHS (RIN 1653-AB01) fixa US$70.000 por estudante F-1 no OPT inicial e US$30.000 em qualquer OPT subsequente, incluindo a extensão STEM. A escola (DSO) teria de pagar a taxa antes de registrar a recomendação de OPT no SEVIS, e o USCIS não concederia a autorização de trabalho (I-765) sem o pagamento. A regra permite que a escola repasse o custo a estudantes ou empregadores.

É apenas uma proposta: entraria em vigor 60 dias após a publicação de uma regra final. O texto indica comentários até 09/11/2026 (a coleta de informações do PRA, até 07/12); o registro eletrônico do Federal Register mostra datas divergentes, então confirme no PDF oficial.
